accepted.evidence: Turner 5193 jānā́ti 'knows' explicitly gives European and Armenian Romani ǰan-; the printed source has Zargari nā́-džān-āvās 'I did not know' (p. 130 §2.5.3). The source explicitly identifies stressed nā- as its negative prefix, and p. 139 §3.7.1 identifies -āvās as first-person singular imperfect. The inherited know stem is the target; negative and person-tense morphology are retained in the attestation. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.

Turner 12598 śr̥ṇṓti 'hears' explicitly gives European Romani šun-; the printed source has Zargari nā-šundās 'he did not hear' (p. 144 §3.20.4.1), explicitly under its nā- negative prefix. The source describes -d as a perfect-stem marker after n (p. 138 §3.6.2) and -ās as the third-person singular perfect ending (p. 139 §3.7.1). The inherited hear stem matches the diagnostic Romani comparison. Original PDF, glyph-decoded source audit and imported key checked; no transcription or identity change.
